reasoning: Every clause of the turn is the same act: the person sees shell commands running and wants to know what they are. 'что тут за шеллы бегут', 'это просто программы', 'ты все продумал, они просто уже код гоняют', 'какой' are four phrasings of one question, not four acts - none of them says anything the neighbouring one's goal does not already carry, so under the grounds rule they stay one act. Nothing is asked for, nothing is reported that was not already visible on screen, and no work is in flight whose goal is being changed. A question creates nothing and changes no document: the Director may read, or send a reader, to answer accurately - what runs, why it was started, what it is doing - but must not turn the question into a task because answering it took effort. So no decision sheet, no checkpoint, no dimension named, no specialist called. The reply is one thing: answered.
